item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports testing the loss before changing SASRec’s encoder. [gSASRec’s IJCAI 2024 extended abstract](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf), based on the 2023 paper, attributes substantial weakness to negative-sampling-induced overconfidence; it recommends 128–256 negatives and generalized BCE with t=0.75. This corrects sampling-related calibration, not false-negative labels. [Scalable Cross-Entropy, RecSys 2024](https://doi.org/10.1145/3640457.3688140), approximates full-catalog softmax using informative, high-inner-product candidates, reporting up to 100× lower peak memory. The [2026 RecArena repository](https://github.com/amazon-science/RecArena) provides a systematic comparison framework for full CE, sampled softmax, BCE and gBCE; its README alone does not establish a winner for this task.\n\nHard negatives can also be plausible unobserved positives. Earlier [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) addresses this through teacher-provided soft labels and consistency regularization. Practical experiment proposal: compare single-negative BCE against multi-negative gBCE and sampled-softmax listwise competition, then add a modest hard-negative mixture after warm-up. Exclude padding, the target and observed training-history positives; deduplicate candidates. Treat downweighting uncertain hard negatives as an ablation, since model confidence does not establish relevance. Use only training interactions for these controls. None of these sources establishes an Electronics-specific gain under the pinned RecHarness protocol: select using fixed four-category macro validation HR@10, inspect category results, and account for GPU cost. Larger training margins alone do not demonstrate better recommendation."}
